topics.topic: Applicability and precedence of upstream_failed versus skipped_by_guard
questions: What exact scope makes both statuses apply: failures and guard-disabled inputs anywhere on the same node, only competing causes on the same input port, or also an upstream failure on an edge to a constant-fed port?

What exactly makes `upstream_failed` applicable, especially when an edge from a failed upstream node is guarded and would otherwise be disabled: does any failed source connected to the node win, only a failed source on the affected input port, or only a failed source whose edge was required to deliver?

quotes:
A node an
   input of which comes from a failed node, or from a node itself
   `upstream_failed`, concludes `upstream_failed` without executing; when both
   rule 4 and this rule apply, this rule wins.

A node with one input from a failed node and another whose only edge is
   disabled by its guard concludes `upstream_failed`, not `skipped_by_guard`.

a port with a constant has no other
      constant and no edge;
judgement.why: State 2 makes precedence node-wide across input ports, propagates upstream_failed from failed or upstream_failed sources, and forbids an edge to a constant-fed port.

topics.topic: Scope of the constant-fed input exemption from guard-based node skipping
questions: Is the constant exception only per input port, so another input port that can no longer receive a value still makes the node `skipped_by_guard`, or does any constant-fed input prevent that node status?

Does this exempt only that input port from causing `skipped_by_guard`, while another input port can still make the node `skipped_by_guard`, or does any constant-fed port prevent the whole node from being skipped?

quotes:
An input port that can no longer receive a value because every edge into
   it is disabled, or comes from a skipped node, makes its node `skipped_by_guard`
   without executing; this applies transitively and to flow outputs, which are
   then reported `skipped_by_guard` (A05 rule 4).
judgement.why: State 2 treats availability per input port, so a constant satisfies its own port but does not prevent another unavailable port from skipping the node.

topics.topic: Whether constants and edges may share an input port and how their outcomes are resolved
questions: May an input port fed by a constant also have incoming edges, and if so which source supplies the port when an edge can deliver?
May one input port be targeted by both a FlowConstant and one or more FlowEdges, and if so which source supplies its value and how do failure or guard outcomes on the edges affect the node?

quotes:
fan-in, by (`to_node`, `to_port`): every input port of every node, and every
      flow output, has at least one source; a port with a constant has no other
      constant and no edge; and no two edges that can both deliver (rule 3) end at
      the same port, whatever its cardinality;
judgement.why: State 2 explicitly forbids a constant and any edge from sharing an input port.

topics.topic: Which source execution statuses count as skipped and whether upstream_failed propagates transitively
questions: Does “skipped node” mean only a node recorded `skipped_by_guard`, or also one recorded `upstream_failed`; consequently, does `upstream_failed` propagate transitively through downstream nodes or become `skipped_by_guard` after one hop?
Which NodeExecution statuses make a source count as a "skipped node" for this rule: only `skipped_by_guard`, or also `upstream_failed` (or any non-executed source)?

quotes:
A node an
   input of which comes from a failed node, or from a node itself
   `upstream_failed`, concludes `upstream_failed` without executing; when both
   rule 4 and this rule apply, this rule wins.

`skipped_by_guard` when every edge into it was disabled by its guard or comes
   from a node recorded `skipped_by_guard`, otherwise `not_produced`.
judgement.why: State 2 limits skipped-source propagation to nodes recorded skipped_by_guard and separately makes upstream_failed propagate transitively.

topics.topic: Whether guard and upstream-skip handling for mapped nodes is per node or per map_index
questions: For a mapped node, is inability to receive a value evaluated for the whole node or separately for each `map_index`, and what happens when only some mapped elements are disabled or come from skipped upstream executions?
